 1               CROSS REBUTTAL TESTIMONY OF J. LUTHER KING, JR.
 2                 ON BEHALF OF 4K LAND AND CATTLE COMPANY


 3                        I.   INTRODUCTION AND OUALIFICATIONS

 4   Q.      PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME AND BUSINESS ADDRESS.

 5   A.      My name is J. Luther King, Jr. My business address is 301 Commerce Street

 6           Suite 1600, Fort Worth, Texas 76102.

 7   Q.      ARE YOU THE SAME J. LUTHER KING, JR. THAT FILED DIRECT

 8           TESTIMONY IN THIS PROCEEDING ON MAY 13, 2026?

 9   A.      Yes, I am.

10   Q.      WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR CROSS-REBUTTAL TESTIMONY?

11   A.      I am responding to the direct testimony of Jason E. Buntz on behalf of Colorado

12           River Alliance Intervenors, filed as Item 4319 on May 13, 2026. Mr. Buntz

13           recommends Route 894 over routes in the Northern Corridor. Mr. Buntz concludes

14           that routes in the Northern Corridor are "generally longer and more expensive" and

15           do not perform as well on certain quantitative metrics. Based on my direct

16           experience owning and managing land along both the Northern Corridor and the

17           Route 894 corridor in McCulloch County, I disagree with the suggestion that the

18           Northern Corridor is inferior to Route 894.

19                    As stated in my direct testimony, I support routes that follow existing civic

20           or industrial infrastructure corridors, such as large highways. The Northern

21           Corridor is one such group of routes, as these routes generally run in close

22           proximity to large highways, including United States (US) highway 190. Northern

23           Corridor routes that appear to be superior options include Routes 416, 410, 392,

     Cross Rebuttal Testimony of J. Luther King, Jr. on Behalf of 4K Land and Cattle Company
     Docket No. 59475
                                                                                                Page 2 of 5




 1           402, 391, 589, 592, 74, 93, and 100. This list is based on the analysis of expert

 2           witness James E. Scott, III, who filed direct testimony on behalf of 4K Land and

 3           Cattle Company in this proceeding.

 4   Q.      WAS THIS TESTIMONY PREPARED BY YOU OR UNDER YOUR

 5           DIRECTION?

 6   A.      Yes.

 7   Q.      IS YOUR TESTIMONY TRUE AND CORRECT TO THE BEST OF YOUR

 8           KNOWLEDGE?

 9   A.      Yes.



10                                 II. RESPONSE TO MR. BUNTZ

11   Q.      HAVE       YOU       REVIEWED          MR.      BUNTZ'S        DIRECT        TESTIMONY

12           REGARDING THE NORTHERN CORRIDOR?

13   A.      Yes. Mr. Buntz is the Operations Manager for Hicks & Company, an environmental

14           consulting firm in Austin, Texas. He presents a largely quantitative comparison of

15           the five corridors identified in the Application, including the Northern Corridor

16           (defined by routes using Link U6), and concludes that Route 894 - a Link J27

17           Corridor route - best balances the PUC routing criteria under PURA § 37.056(c)(4)

18           and PUC Subst. R. § 25.101(b)(3)(B).

19   Q.      DO YOU HAVE CONCERNS WITH MR. BUNTZ'S ANALYSIS AS

20           APPLIED TO THE NORTHERN CORRIDOR?

21   A.      I do. While I do not take issue with Mr. Buntz' s numerical data as presented, his

22           analysis is incomplete because it is purely quantitative. It does not account for


     Cross Rebuttal Testimony of J. Luther King, Jr. on Behalf of 4K Land and Cattle Company
     Docket No. 59475
                                                                                                Page 3 of 5




 1           qualitative differences in the land along these corridors - differences that are

 2           apparent to someone who actually owns and manages property along both the

 3           proposed Northern Corridor and the proposed Route 894/Link J27 Corridor.

 4                    Mr. Buntz' s analysis relies entirely on the Kimley-Horn and Halff

 5           Environmental Assessment data tables, publicly available maps and datasets, aerial

 6           photography, and a single site visit on December 16, 2025 to "areas along the

 7           corridor of routes using Link J31" - which is neither the Northern Corridor nor the

 8           Route 894 corridor in McCulloch County. Based on his testimony, he did not visit

 9           McCulloch County. He did not observe the terrain along the Northern Corridor or

10           the Route 894 corridor where 4K Ranch' s property is located. His testimony does

11           not reflect any firsthand knowledge of the conditions along either corridor in the

12           portion of the Study Area where our property lies.

13   Q.      PLEASE         EXPLAIN         WHAT         YOU       MEAN         BY     QUALITATIVE

14           DIFFERENCES.

15   A.      I estimate that the Northern Corridor Routes 416, 410, 392, 402, 391, 589, 592, 74,

16           93, and 100 would cut through approximately 10.4 miles of my property, and the

17           Route 894 corridor would cut through approximately 11 miles of my property.

18           Based on my ownership of property along both corridors, I am in a position to

19           compare the two corridors based on firsthand knowledge of the land in McCulloch

20           County. The land along the Northern Corridor in McCulloch County is qualitatively

21           better suited for transmission line siting than Mr. Buntz's purely quantitative

22           analysis suggests.




     Cross Rebuttal Testimony of J. Luther King, Jr. on Behalf of 4K Land and Cattle Company
     Docket No. 59475
                                                                                                Page 4 of 5




 1                    The terrain along the 4K Ranch on the Northern Corridor is characterized

 2           by gently rolling rangeland, accessible terrain, minimal steep grades, established

 3           ranch roads, less erosion-prone soils, and fewer sensitive riparian crossings. By

 4           contrast, portions of the Route 894 corridor along the 4K Ranch is comparatively

 5           less suitable.    For example, in comparison to the Northern Corridor, the more

 6           southern terrain is rougher, has more erosion, and contains many bluffs and rocks.

 7           I expect the terrain would be challenging for construction because there are many

 8           areas where a road cannot be reasonably constructed. In short, common sense

 9           would suggest avoiding the more southern areas because the terrain is significantly

10           less suitable in these areas compared to the Northern Corridor as each crosses the

11           4K Ranch. The quantitative metrics in Mr. Buntz' s testimony - cost, length, and

12           percentage of paralleling - do not capture these on-the-ground differences in terrain

13           suitability, soil stability, construction accessibility, and long-term maintainability.

14   Q.      DOES YOUR OWNERSHIP OF LAND ALONG BOTH CORRIDORS

15           AFFECT YOUR PERSPECTIVE?

16   A.      I believe it makes my perspective more balanced, not less. 4K Ranch has a

17           substantial ownership stake along both the Route 392 and Route 894 corridors -

18           approximately 10.4 miles on the former and approximately 11 miles on the latter.

19           We are not advocating for one route over the other because of a one-sided property

20           interest. Our position is based on direct familiarity with the conditions along both

21           routes in McCulloch County, and our experience is that the northern corridor

22           presents qualitatively superior conditions for transmission line construction and

23           long-term operation.

     Cross Rebuttal Testimony of J. Luther King, Jr. on Behalf of 4K Land and Cattle Company
     Docket No. 59475
                                                                                               Page 5 of 5




1   Q.      DOES THIS TESTIMONY INDICATE A CHANGE IN YOUR POSITION

2           WITH RESPECT TO THE ROUTE ADEQUACY CHALLENGE?

3   A.      No. We continue to support our route adequacy challenge. This testimony and

4           recommendation are subj ect to, and do not constitute a waiver of, that challenge.



5                                        III.     CONCLUSION

6   Q.      DOES THIS CONCLUDE YOUR TESTIMONY?

7   A.      Yes.
